verdict.rationale: Weave's marketing site says built-in and custom signals automatically classify agent interactions, and that alerts can trigger webhook automations. That is a product-owned background automation, but it is described only in a single marketing line, with no first-party guide on setting it up. The 'automatic iteration loops' run by Claude Code via MCP are driven by an external coding agent, so they are a user-side arrangement and are not credited. Missing for 10: documented setup and configuration of automations, recurring or scheduled background jobs, trigger and action options beyond alert webhooks, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Built-in and custom signals automatically capture and classify agent interactions, so you always know how your agents are behaving. Alerts route what matters through Slack notifications and trigger webhook automations
